name: Steam locomotive
title: Steam locomotive (0-6-0 tank engine)
intro: This is an 0-6-0 steam tank engine. Explode it (🧩) to see the firebox, boiler tubes, cylinders and Walschaerts valve gear. Ask me "How does steam turn the wheels?"
suggest: How does steam turn the wheels?
Why are the left and right cranks 90° apart?
How does a steam engine go backwards?
looksLike: train, steam train, locomotive, steam engine, railway vehicle, rails

wheelset_1.name: Leading driving wheels
wheelset_1.info: Front pair of driving wheels. On an 0-6-0, all three wheel pairs are linked by coupling rods to pull together.

wheelset_2.name: Main driving wheels
wheelset_2.info: Center driving wheels pushed directly by the main connecting rods, which also drive the valve gear via a return crank.

wheelset_3.name: Trailing driving wheels
wheelset_3.info: Rear pair of driving wheels driven in sync by the coupling rods.

cylinder_l.name: Left cylinder
cylinder_l.info: High-pressure steam enters alternately in front of and behind the piston, driving it back and forth.

piston_l.name: Left piston
piston_l.info: Pushed back and forth inside the cylinder by steam to drive the crosshead via the piston rod.

crosshead_l.name: Left crosshead
crosshead_l.info: Slides straight along guide bars, taking the side load of the swinging connecting rod so the piston rod stays straight.

connecting_rod_l.name: Left connecting rod
connecting_rod_l.info: Links the crosshead to the main wheel's crank pin, converting linear push-pull into wheel rotation.

coupling_rod_l.name: Left coupling rod
coupling_rod_l.info: Connects the crank pins of all three wheelsets so they turn and pull in unison.

valve_l.name: Left valve
valve_l.info: Switches steam passages to feed either the front or back of the piston while exhausting used steam from the other side.

eccentric_rod_l.name: Left eccentric rod
eccentric_rod_l.info: Driven by the main wheel's return crank to rock the expansion link and time the steam valve.

expansion_link_l.name: Left expansion link
expansion_link_l.info: Curved rocking link. Moving the die block between its top and bottom halves reverses the train and adjusts steam cutoff.

radius_rod_l.name: Left radius rod
radius_rod_l.info: Transfers motion from the expansion link to the combination lever; raised or lowered by the reverser.

combination_lever_l.name: Left combination lever
combination_lever_l.info: Combines motions from the expansion link and crosshead to actuate the steam valve at the exact right moment.

union_link_l.name: Left union link
union_link_l.info: Links the crosshead to the bottom of the combination lever.

cylinder_r.name: Right cylinder
cylinder_r.info: Right cylinder where high-pressure steam pushes both sides of the piston in turn.

piston_r.name: Right piston
piston_r.info: Reciprocates back and forth inside the right cylinder under steam pressure.

crosshead_r.name: Right crosshead
crosshead_r.info: Slides along straight guide bars between the piston rod and connecting rod to prevent bending.

connecting_rod_r.name: Right connecting rod
connecting_rod_r.info: Converts the right crosshead's straight push into rotation of the main driving wheels.

coupling_rod_r.name: Right coupling rod
coupling_rod_r.info: Links the crank pins of all three right-side driving wheels.

valve_r.name: Right valve
valve_r.info: Controls admission and exhaust of steam at both ends of the right cylinder.

eccentric_rod_r.name: Right eccentric rod
eccentric_rod_r.info: Driven by the right main wheel's return crank to rock the right expansion link.

expansion_link_r.name: Right expansion link
expansion_link_r.info: Right curved link that sets forward or reverse valve timing.

radius_rod_r.name: Right radius rod
radius_rod_r.info: Carries motion from the right expansion link to the combination lever.

combination_lever_r.name: Right combination lever
combination_lever_r.info: Combines link and crosshead motions to drive the right steam valve.

union_link_r.name: Right union link
union_link_r.info: Connects the right crosshead to the bottom of the right combination lever.

frames.name: Frames
frames.info: Heavy twin steel frame plates supporting the boiler, cylinders and wheelsets.

firebox.name: Firebox
firebox.info: Furnace where coal burns, sending hot gas forward through the boiler tubes.

boiler_tubes.name: Boiler tubes
boiler_tubes.info: Over a hundred fire tubes running through the boiler water, creating a huge surface area to boil water fast.

steam_pipes.name: Steam pipes
steam_pipes.info: Pipes routing high-pressure steam from the top of the boiler through the regulator to both cylinders.

blastpipe.name: Blastpipe
blastpipe.info: Blasts used steam up the chimney, creating suction that draws fresh air into the firebox and makes the "chuff" sound.

reverser.name: Reverser
reverser.info: Cab mechanism that shifts the expansion link die block to switch between forward and reverse and adjust steam cutoff.

regulator.name: Regulator
regulator.info: The locomotive's throttle valve, controlling how much steam flows from the boiler into the cylinders.

track.name: Track
track.info: Steel rails. Flanges on the inner rim of the wheels keep the train guided along the track.

footplate.name: Running board
footplate.info: Walkway platform along the top of the frame for maintenance access.

boiler_cladding.name: Boiler cladding
boiler_cladding.info: Insulated sheet-metal casing that keeps heat inside the boiler. Explode (🧩) to see the firebox and tubes.

smokebox.name: Smokebox and chimney
smokebox.info: Front chamber where smoke from the boiler tubes collects before being drawn up the chimney by the steam blast.

smokebox_door.name: Smokebox door
smokebox_door.info: Hinged round front door opened after runs to shovel out collected soot and ash.

tank_l.name: Left water tank
tank_l.info: Side water tank feeding the boiler. Carrying water on the engine itself makes this a "tank engine" that needs no tender.

tank_r.name: Right water tank
tank_r.info: Right-side water tank interconnected with the left tank for balanced weight.

cab.name: Cab
cab.info: Crew compartment where the fireman shovels coal into the firebox and the driver operates the regulator and reverser.

cab_roof.name: Cab roof
cab_roof.info: Hinged cab roof that lifts open to view the interior controls.

drives.run: Running forward (cylinders → connecting rods → three pairs of wheels)
drives.open: Opening the smokebox door and cab roof

steps.say: Hot gas from burning coal flows through over a hundred boiler tubes, boiling the surrounding water into high-pressure steam.

quiz.q: What flows inside the locomotive's boiler tubes?
options: Hot gas from the firebox
In a fire-tube boiler, hot gas runs inside the tubes to heat the water surrounding them.
Boiler water
Water surrounds the outside of the tubes; water-inside-tubes is a water-tube boiler used in power plants.
High-pressure steam
Steam rises to the top of the boiler shell and leaves through the steam pipes.

steps.say: Opening the regulator sends high-pressure steam through the steam pipes into both cylinders.
Steam pushes the piston and rod, sliding the crosshead straight back and forth along its guide bars.

quiz.q: Why connect the piston rod to a sliding crosshead instead of directly to the wheel's connecting rod?
options: To absorb sideways forces from the swinging rod so the piston rod stays straight
Without the crosshead taking the side load, the swinging connecting rod would bend the piston rod and ruin the cylinder seal.
To steer the locomotive
Wheel flanges against the rails steer the train, not the crosshead.
To increase steam pressure
Steam pressure comes from boiling water in the boiler; the crosshead is purely mechanical.

steps.say: The main connecting rod turns linear push-pull into rotation of the main wheels, and coupling rods drive the front and rear pairs.

quiz.q: Why are the right-side crank pins offset 90° ahead of the left-side ones?
options: So both sides never hit dead centre at once, ensuring the train can always start
If both sides were in step and stopped on dead centre (crank and rod in a straight line), neither side could push to start.
For visual symmetry
The 90° offset is there to avoid dead centre; looks have nothing to do with it.
To increase top speed
Top speed depends on steam supply and wheel diameter; the offset is for reliable starting.

valve.title: Valve gear: when the steam goes in

steps.say: As the main wheel turns, its return crank pushes and pulls the eccentric rod to rock the expansion link.
The radius rod passes that rocking motion to the combination lever, which adds crosshead position to move the steam valve.
Sliding back and forth, the valve feeds fresh steam to one side of the piston while venting used steam from the other.

quiz.q: While the piston is being pushed forward, which side of the piston is receiving high-pressure steam?
options: Behind it, pushing it forward
The valve admits fresh steam behind the piston while opening the front port to exhaust used steam.
In front of it
Steam in front would push the piston backward, not forward.
Both sides equally
Equal pressure on both sides would cancel out and stall the piston.

steps.say: To reverse, the driver shifts the radius rod to the opposite half of the expansion link, flipping valve timing so the wheels turn backward.

quiz.q: How does a steam locomotive go in reverse?
options: Use the reverser to flip the valve timing
Shifting the die block to the other half of the expansion link reverses when steam enters the cylinders.
Shift into a reverse gear in a gearbox
Steam locomotives have no gearbox; they reverse the pistons directly via valve timing.
Steam locomotives cannot reverse
They run equally well in both directions and shunt cars back and forth all the time.

steps.say: Used steam from the cylinders blasts upward through the blastpipe at the base of the chimney.
Each steam blast pulls air out of the smokebox, drawing fresh oxygen into the firebox so the fire burns hotter the faster the train runs.

quiz.q: How many "chuff" exhaust sounds come from the chimney for each full turn of the wheels?
options: 4 chuffs
Two cylinders, and each one exhausts once from the front and once from the back: 4 per turn.
1 chuff
Double-acting cylinders exhaust on both forward and backward strokes.
2 chuffs
That only counts one cylinder—both left and right cylinders exhaust twice per turn.

steps.say: Open the front smokebox door to see the blastpipe right below the chimney, drafting the fire with every puff.

rods_off.title: The coupling rods came off
rods_off.symptom: Steam is driving the pistons and the middle wheels spin, but the front and rear wheel pairs stay still. What's broken?
rods_off.hint: The main connecting rod only pushes the middle wheelset. What horizontal rod normally links all three wheelsets together?
suspects: The wheels are stuck on the track
rods_off.observe: Look at the crank pins on the middle wheels and compare them with the front and rear wheels: what link between them is missing?
whys: Watch the cylinders and main rods—they're pushing strongly and spinning the middle wheels fine. Look at what connects the wheels to each other.
Nothing is jamming the wheels on the rails—they simply aren't receiving any force. Check the crank pins on the outside of all three wheelsets.
rods_off.cause: The coupling rods on both sides came off, so the main rods only turn the middle wheels and nothing drives the front and rear pairs.
rods_off.why: Why do only the middle wheels turn when the coupling rods come off?
rods_off.answer: The main connecting rods only drive the middle wheelset; the front and rear wheels rely on the coupling rods linking their crank pins to turn together.
reasons: The coupling rods are pipes that carry steam to the front and rear wheels.
The front and rear wheels only turn by rail friction, and coupling rods are just decorative.
